summary: Wrote the ES_Q1 Type II analogue as a fixed-entry SL2(Z[i]) count ([[a,n],[c,d]], ad−nc=1, c∈4Z[i], quadrant conditions on a,d): a Bianchi spectral count (EGM Ch. 5) counts Γ-elements in growing norm balls, and at a fixed top-right entry n it reduces to Σ_c #{d | nc+1, d ≡ −1 mod c} — the same polylog divisor lottery, whose main term is a product of local densities times an archimedean (quadrant) volume. The 2-adic density of 4uBC−u−B=n is uniform in n (4uC−1 is a 2-adic unit, so B is determined), so a spectral main term can only see the observed low-count cell Im n ≡ 1 (4) (Z52_BANKED T4) through the quadrant/2-adic coupling already measured empirically there; nothing at the six failures (N ≤ 5393) is predicted beyond 'low-count cell'.

Exradii claim checked (s² = r_a r_b + r_b r_c + r_c r_a, tangent lengths r_a r_b/s > 0, so every positive triple is a triangle; the equivalence with ES is a pure rephrasing). The rational/Heronian strengthening (s² = XY+YZ+ZX a square ⇔ nXYZ = □) FAILS at every prime p ≡ 1 (4): CERTIFIED for all n ≤ 3000 that it holds iff 4 | n or n has a prime factor ≡ 3 (4) (exact match, 525 failing n), and PROVED for primes p ≡ 1 (4) by a 10-line descent (Type II forces p | X; Type I forces p = h(4t²yz−1)/(y+z) with gcd(4t²yz−1, y+z) | (2ty)²+1, so the cofactor dividing p is ≡ 3 (4)). So the triangle variant is a χ₋₄-killed dead variant (like the altitude variant Z1931), with no new handle on the hard primes; integer-side (Heronian) variant additionally fails sporadically for 50 n ≤ 3000 with 3-mod-4 factors.

The first step is already DONE in the repo (scripts/z52b_translate_cheap.py part (a)): the integer-altitude variant (smallest denominator x > p/2) fails at every prime p ≡ 1 (4). I re-checked the proof sketch: Type II is impossible (1/a+1/b > 2), and in Type I with z = kp, 4k−1 = jp, the two small denominators satisfy x ≤ p/2 + 1/(2j) < p/2 + 1/2, impossible for odd p unless j = 1, which needs p ≡ 3 (4). Nothing further in the item (the alt steps re-measure a fraction that is provably 0 at hard primes).

Computed (sympy) disc_T(4T²(T−s)+e(4T−n)) = −16e(64e² + 27en² − 72ens − 16es² + 16ns³) (generic S₃), and showed that a rational root x fixes e = 4x²(s−x)/(4x−n), after which total splitting ⇔ (4x−n)(x−s)(ns+3nx−4sx+4x²) is a square — i.e. the split locus is exactly the image of U_n under Vieta (birational), and the square condition is the usual 'm y z = M(y+z)' divisor problem in disguise. Bookkeeping: for prime n every solution has n | xyz, so 4 | e₂. Hilbert-irreducibility/Schinzel-type split-value counts give upper (density-zero) bounds, not lower bounds at fixed n; nothing new.

BRAINSTORM/z45_siegel_dichotomy.md §§2.2–2.3 already does exactly this: Heath-Brown 1983 verified, the exceptional term worked out in the forced-window orthogonality count (it raises the count of sign/window candidates only when χ_D = χ_p, and is class-dependent otherwise), and the orientation measured on all 332 180 primes p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 10⁷ (pretence χ_p ≈ 1 makes certificates harder; χ_D ≈ −1 bias acts on free primes, not on the factor multiset of a prescribed K_q = (p+q)/4). Friedlander–Iwaniec IMRN 2003 no. 37 exists (verified, OUP abstract) and gives AP asymptotics for primes under a strong exceptional-character hypothesis — again an average over primes, so it adds nothing pointwise beyond z45's analysis; answer to the first step: no, a Siegel zero does not force large p with χ_D(p)=1 into a forcing line.

Both halves are already in the repo: the 'universal family of levels' hitting-set measurement is BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md (least certificate-family size s(p) for Mordell-class primes to 10⁸, max 2814, CRT-avoidance law δ(X) ≈ exp(−0.028(ln X)³), conjectured growth exp(((ln x)/c)^{1/3})), and any finite family fails by Mordell–Schinzel/H4_NOT_POLYLOG (lower bounds exp((log p)^κ)). The complexity side is HARDNESS_MAP A5 / BREADTH_Z45 §9 and BRAINSTORM/z31_complexity.md: a deterministic poly(log p) ES solver at primes yields deterministic QNR finding (open without GRH), and polylog-height reduced witnesses fail infinitely often (A4, Graham–Ringrose). Nothing beyond these in the item.

Structural check instead of a LattE run (LattE not installed, and the set is not polyhedral): at fixed level C the certificates are the divisor pairs of 4Cp+1 on a hyperbola, so any dyadic polyhedral approximation contains essentially all lattice points and the equality constraint is lost; at fixed (u,C) B is a single value, so a polyhedral encoding needs ≍ p log p pieces (the trial form). Moreover the family S_n = {(u,B,C) ∈ ℕ³ : 4uBC−u−B = n} is provably NOT parametric-Presburger: by Woods' theorem (parametric Presburger counting) |S_n| would be eventually quasi-polynomial in n, but R(n) ≤ n^{o(1)} forces a bounded quasi-polynomial while R(p) is unbounded (FRONTIER §2.2 Prop 3.1, Linnik). So Barvinok/Woods short generating functions cannot carry p as a parameter; at fixed p the set is finite (polylog size) and computing its GF is equivalent to finding the divisors, i.e. no speed-up for weighted sign sums.
evidence: Woods, Presburger arithmetic, rational generating functions, and quasi-polynomials, J. Symb. Logic 80 (2015) (parametric Presburger counts eventually quasi-polynomial); survey arXiv:1308.4694 (abstract verified via arXiv API: even the conjectural 'unreasonable' extension keeps variables linear, which 4uBC excludes)

summary: Literature check done: the residue-class analogue is classical — Erdős, 'On the distribution of divisors of integers in the residue classes (mod d)' (1965, renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-10.pdf), Thm 1: for k < 2^{(1−ε) log log x} = (log x)^{(1−ε)log 2}, almost all n < x have a divisor in EVERY class l (mod k), and this is sharp by Hardy–Ramanujan (Thm 4 even gives equidistribution of divisor counts between classes); 'class-propinquity' a ≡ −b (mod e) with ab | N is the same subset-product statement. For ES the moduli 4C ≤ (log p)^{0.69} admissible in Erdős's range give ≈ (log p)^{0.69} tied integers 4Cp+1, so the theorem only says typical N works — the per-p statement still needs that not all of these tied N are atypical (B2/B6); nothing beyond the many existing Erdős–Hall items (z52b_free_opus 213, z52b_translate 77/84), though the Erdős 1965 citation itself is not yet in the repo's literature notes.

Computed Disp_X(p) = Σ_{C≤X}(D_C − E_C)², E_C = 2τ₃(4Cp+1)/φ(4C) (τ₃ = #divisors ≡ 3 mod 4), for the (★)-failure p = 8 813 281 and a control p = 1 000 033, X = 10…10⁴. Disp saturates by X ≈ 300 (≈ 17 and ≈ 39: it is dominated by C ≤ 30), while M_X grows only like ≈ 8·log X, so the Cauchy–Schwarz dispersion ratio X·Disp/M_X² is ≥ 0.4 at its best (X = 10, control prime) and grows ∝ X/log X (≈ 60–120 at X = 10⁴); no θ with X = p^θ gives R > 0, because each D_C is a 0/τ-valued rare event and the family mean is polylog (Linnik's mechanism needs a family whose total mean dominates its length). Side observation: at the failing prime the uniform model still predicts M_X ≈ 52 against R_X = 0, i.e. the deficit sits in the BM/genus layer the model ignores, not in dispersion.

Re-read SINGLE_P_COUNT §4.1–4.2: the log-log loss is in Prop 4.1 (GRH used only to find primes ℓ ≤ p/6 with two prescribed character values, i.e. a single-family genus witness), and the item's premise is outdated — BM_CORRECTED_COUNT Thm 2.2 now gives the main term M_BM(p) ≫ (log p)² unconditionally (∼ M₀ under GRH). The 'which GRH-type statement suffices' question is answered by the §4.2 table: what is missing is the order-≥3 character sum X(p) = Σ_q φ(q)⁻¹Σ_χ χ(p)χ̄(a) at ONE argument over ≍ p log p moduli, which is the dual of what GRH (fixed χ, sum over n) controls; Hooley's GRH proof of p + x² + y² is a fixed-character / long-family dispersion of exactly the dual type, so 'GRH + pair correlation' or GRH for higher-order characters does not change this. Nothing new in the item.

SIGN_IDENTITY.md already ran the Tunnell/Waldspurger route (Prop 2.4: weight-3/2 eigenforms with non-square-conductor Shimura lift vanish on whole root-number classes of n ≡ 3 (4), where N₋ ≥ 1 is proved; square conductors open) and a certified linear-relation screen including ternary theta coefficients r_Q for six forms (§3: no relation, any class mod 8, n ≤ 12 000). The two 0/1 variants the item proposes are degenerate: N₋(p) is always EVEN for p ≡ 1 (4) (the involution (t,u,v) ↦ (t,v,u) preserves χ since AA* = tp+1 ≡ 1 (mod p), and its only fixed word at a prime, u = v = 1, has χ = (−1/p) = +1; checked numerically for all 67 primes < 800), and [λ(p) ≤ 3] is identically 1 on all tested primes, so a Tunnell-shaped identity only has content on composite n (zero set = odd squares ∪ {105}, i.e. the Prop 2.4 square-conductor case).

Short proof attempt settles it: the S-integral ladder is degenerate. For ANY nonempty S (any prime q ∈ S) and every n, take a solution of 4/q = 1/a + 1/b + 1/c (exists for every prime q; e.g. 4/5 = 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/20) and set x = an/q, y = bn/q, z = cn/q ∈ ℤ[1/q]_{>0}; then 1/x + 1/y + 1/z = (q/n)(4/q) = 4/n (PROVED, one line; e.g. 4/n = 5/(2n) + 5/(4n) + 1/(4n)). More generally ES over ℤ[1/S](n) ⇔ ES(n·s) for some S-unit s, which always holds. So there is no threshold S between ES (S = ∅) and a trivial problem, and no calibration point.

The first step (compute μ and Δ for the (★) events and compare exp(−μ+Δ/2) with the observed zero probability) is BRAINSTORM/s9_janson_dependency.md: over 108 283 primes p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 3·10⁶, Δ/μ = 3.6 → 9.4 (growing ≈ linearly in μ), so exp(−μ+Δ/2) > 1 and μ²/(2Δ) = 0.85 → 1.82 ≪ log p — word-level Janson is useless; at level granularity E[#hit levels] ≈ (0.44 → 0.97)·log p is exactly critical. The 'derandomised' version (alt step translate-0144) is EXSET_ARITH_JANSON_OPUS.md: integer Janson −log ν ≥ μ − Σ η_i P(E_i) − KΔ holds under one explicit hypothesis (RLD), with a proved square floor (B) showing the RLD error must absorb all mass beyond ½ log N, i.e. exactly where pseudorandomness of p's residues is unproved. Nothing new beyond these.

Read the proof in arXiv:1805.02945 (Thm 3 and its proof): the density-one bound f₃(4,n) ≥ exp((log 6 + o(1)) log log n) = (log n)^{log 6+o(1)} is τ(n/4) ≥ 2^{(1+o(1))ω(n)} choices of a divisor d of n times 3^{ω(n)} two-unit-fraction representations of the cofactor 1/(n(n/d+1)/4…), with ω(n) ∼ log log n (Hardy–Ramanujan/Turán–Kubilius) — i.e. it is pure anatomy of n itself. It gives nothing at primes (ω(p) = 1), and the 'prime-shifted' variant via factors of 4Cp+1 is exactly the per-p lower-tail problem (B2/B6); EP's Remark 1 already uses shifts of n for their infinitely-many-n bound. Also the item's target is mis-specified: 2 is not the conjectured almost-all exponent for all n (the mean over n is ≍ log³ n), so there is no 'log 6 → 2' gap to close.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.02945 (Thm 3, proof §6, Remarks 1 and 3; PDF read)

summary: MARKOFF_ES.md §1 already tabulates Ghosh–Sarnak, Loughran–Mitankin (arXiv:1807.10223: Thm 1.3 BM-obstructed m − 4 ∈ ⟨±1,2,3,5⟩ mod squares; Thm 1.4/1.5 counts of BM-explained and non-BM failures; Br U_m/Br ℚ ≅ (ℤ/2)³) and Colliot-Thélène–Wei–Xu side by side with the ES surfaces, and §2 answers the 'which steps use the Vieta group' question: on the ES-related surfaces S_{n,D}: nA² + B² + D = ABC both Vieta involutions fix C, so the Markoff group acts fibrewise as a Pell automorph with no mixing and no compact fundamental set (Prop 2.1(b)), and the closure has an A₂ singularity (not Markoff-type); Br is (ℤ/2)², purely algebraic (Prop 2.2). The repo note's 'not reconciled with ES' is outdated relative to this file; the ES content is the side condition 2D | C (B2), which LM/CTWX/GS do not see.
evidence: MARKOFF_ES.md §1 (literature, checked against arXiv full texts), §2 Props 2.1–2.2, §3

summary: Did the comparison (Tao arXiv:1909.03562, verified earlier in data/z52b/upgrades_verify_out_4.md): Tao's input is Fourier decay of the Syracuse random variable mod 3^k, i.e. equidistribution of Syr(N) for N drawn log-uniformly from an interval, giving only logarithmic density 1 with no rate, and the per-orbit statement fails because one orbit carries no averaging. ES is strictly ahead on both axes: its exceptional set already has a quasi-power saving (E(N) ≪ N exp(−c(log N)^{3/4}), FRONTIER §1), and per-n it has exact algebraic structure Collatz lacks (BM main term M_BM ≫ log²p, theta-quotient Thm K, T1). Tao's averaging lemma has no smoothing step that acts at a single n, so the side-by-side gives no new lever — both walls are the same quantifier (B6) and ES's extra structure is what the campaign already exploits.

Ran the exact (no SAT needed) coverage computation: the union of residue classes of Type I/II families with modulus | M (scripts/z52b_p1_H06_menu_cover.py) leaves exactly Mordell's 6 square classes mod 840, but mod 9240 / 10920 / 27720 / 120120 it leaves 4 / 10 / 8 / 62 NON-square unit classes uncovered (mod 9240: 2041, 2521, 3361, 5161, all non-residues mod 11; their lifts to 9240·k stay largely uncovered for k ≤ 17), and squares are never covered. This is already the repo's 'complete levels' result: BRAINSTORM/z28_complete_levels.md (certified: complete levels ≤ 6000 are all 7-smooth; Thm 2.6 PROVED: no level divisible by a prime ℓ ≡ ±3 (8), ℓ ≥ 11, is complete) and MODEL_SPECIFIC §4.1 (uncovered classes mod 840/9240/120120). Since coverage at a fixed level is an exact union, SAT/ILP would only add minimal-menu (set-cover) sizes, which z52b_dividing's least-family census already measures per prime.

EXSET_FUNCTION_FIELD.md §4.3 and §5.1–5.2 already analyse exactly this: Sawin–Shusterman (Ann. Math. 196 (2022), Thm 1.3) control k-point Chowla only for k < √q/(pe) rank-one (Möbius/character) events, via Pellet's formula making μ(r + s^p) a character in s; at fixed q this is a number of events bounded in q, whereas the FF ES lower tail needs ≍ n (prime family) or ≍ n² (U) events, and the witness counts are traces of covers of rank n!/(s!a!b!), not rank one — the cost model 'depth × log(rank) ≲ (n/2) log q' fails. ff_erdos_straus.md errata adds the B3/B6 reading (square-root savings q^{cn/2} against a poly(n) main term, averages over P). The first step (ES count at fixed prime P as a point count of V_P with controllable top cohomology) is what §4.3 shows lacks a rank-one reduction; nothing new.

Size test (SIGN_IDENTITY word convention): over random samples of 30 primes p ≡ 1 (4) near 10³, 10⁴, 10⁵ the signed count S(p) = N₊ − N₋ has mean |S| = 15.8, 27.7, 36.9, i.e. |S|/log²p ≈ 0.30, 0.30, 0.26 while |S|/log p grows 2.2 → 3.1 (and SIGN_IDENTITY Lemma 2.1 proves log² averages over all n). An ADH-type closed formula — a Hecke-character sum over ideals of norm Ap+B in a FIXED quadratic field, or any finite combination — is bounded by r_K(Ap+B), whose mean over primes is O(1) (Titchmarsh-type, Dedekind-zeta residue), so it cannot match S(p) by size; this extends SIGN_IDENTITY Thm 2.2's holomorphic exclusion to ADH's indefinite-theta/Hecke-character class. A formula would need a field or ideal family growing with p (the level family t, i.e. B2 again).

Heuristic first step answered directly: with M(n) ≍ log²n (for (★)) or ≍ log³n (all ES), the Poisson prediction Σ_{n≤N} exp(−M(n)) converges, so heuristically E(N) = O(1) — a power saving is more than true for ES; for any method that only produces Type I/II solutions, T1 forces E(N) ≥ #{odd squares ≤ N} ≍ N^{1/2}, so δ ≤ 1/2 there. The rest is in the repo: BRAINSTORM/anal_dirichlet_series.md Prop A.1 (σ_E < 1 ⟺ power-saving exceptional set; 'no ES result has one') and B5/T1 bullet (pole of Z at s = 1/2 from odd squares), EXCEPTIONAL_KARY3 / EXCEPTIONAL_LARGESIEVE Thm 3.1 (every CRT/forced-class large-sieve mixture capped at saving C(log N)^{3/4}, so σ_E < 1 needs non-CRT input). MV's Goldbach input (zero density + Siegel-zero case split for primes in APs) has no ES analogue identified beyond those caps; nothing new.
